title: Mejor usar aquello que conoces
excerpt:
Entrada corta. En estos últimos meses, estaba revisando el blog en Substack y
escribiendo algo más a menudo, tratando de trabajarme las entradas y los
artículos. Pero como es esperable, no había muchas visitas. Y al tiempo, de
forma casi casual, revisé blogs antíguos (el primero que abrí debió ser allá por
2006!).

title: On How Everything Becomes a Social Network: The Disease
excerpt:
Many years ago I had a Twitter account. For different reasons, I had some followers
and I was engaged. However, after a couple of years, I realized how much it was
ruining my mood. The amount of interactions with random people, some looking to
vent, others misunderstanding everything everyone could say... I realized the
problem was the format: 160 characters at the time. It was not a place to
discuss, share or answer in nuance ways, with details and understanding. It was
an attention machine.

title: New Development Frameworks, Same Old Shit
excerpt: A new framework has been imposed in another company. And you receive a link to the document that describes how, when and where it will change things… apparently. But when you read it, it is a generic document that could be applied to ANY company. Nothing specific of the company you work from, nothing particular or adapted to the way the company works. A document that the people working on it took a few months to finish, but that you could think it was a template from the internet to apply to your company. But someone forgot to adapt it.

title: Just Another Cycle of Hype
excerpt: Or what poeople like to call it, another bubble. I am talking about AI. And my take, tl;dr is: this is another DotCom bubble, but with new technology.

title: Our Memory is not The Reality
excerpt: Did you notice, at some point in your life, that a memory of some event ended up changing, even in your own recollection? I realized that years ago and it was surprising. I am kind of a story-teller, and one of the main abilities for being one is to create a narrative about the story, diminish parts of the story and amplify others in order to make the story appealing and interesting.

title: When I fell in Love with Computers
excerpt: I was 11 and I didn't have a PC. Many friends had a 386 or even a 486. I was reading PC magazines -PC World is the one I remember the most- for a year or more already. It started out of pure interest, from a child that looked at those machines like something magic. Maybe the reason was the good memories I had with the Spectrum ZX of my uncle when my cousin and I were 8 years old. But I didn't have a computer, it was what it was. Expensive thing those computers.
